stem:
Mihir shades a unit square. He takes $\frac{1}{4}$ of the square and then $\frac{1}{2}$ of that quarter to show $\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{1}{2}$.

Which reading of the shaded product is correct?

options.text: Call the rectangle area the product label, and stop before linking it to the shaded fraction of the unit square.
Shade $\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{1}{2}$ even if the whole region is not the unit square.
The shaded piece is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the unit square, because one half of one quarter is one eighth.
Use the same shading story to find the perimeter of the unit square.

teacher.key_rationale: Half of a quarter of the unit square is one eighth. Naming rectangle area alone, dropping the unit-square whole, or switching to perimeter leave the area-model hinge.
